newsitem.title: USA: Coastal power business earnings to rise.
newsitem.headline: Coastal power business earnings to rise.

text.p: Coastal Corp expects earnings from its international power operations to rise to $100 million in 1999 from $40 million posted by the group last year, Senior Vice President Stirling Pack said on Tuesday.

The Houston-based company also is near agreement on a pact to build a second power plant in Pakistan, where the company currently operates a 100 megawatt facility, he said at the annual Howard Weil energy conference here.
The company expects to announce an agreement on the project "in the not-too-distant future," he said.

The company has forecast solid earnings growth in the coming years, in part from increased sales by its international power business and a turnaround of its refining operations. "I can say we are very much on track to see at least 15 percent earnings growth this year and next," he said.

The company is still in talks on forming a joint venture with Venezuela's Maraven, which would obtain a stake in Coastal's Corpus Christi, Texas refinery in exchange for 80,000 to 120,000 barrels per day of heavy crude oil that would be processed and refined by Coastal.
The company has gradually been shifting its refining slate, and now refines 90.8 percent light products per barrel compared to 75.3 percent in 1992, he said.
